newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL, NEWCASTLE PLAY OUT 4-3 THRILLER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL, NEWCASTLE PLAY OUT 4-3 THRILLER.

text.p: In an amazing case of "deja vu", Liverpool beat Newcastle 4-3 in a soccer classic for the second successive season at Anfield on Monday with the winning goal being scored in injury time.

Almost a year after Liverpool's memorable 4-3 win over Newcastle last April, the two sides produced another breathtaking performance, with Liverpool racing into a 3-0 halftime lead before allowing Newcastle to level at 3-3 with two goals in the last three minutes of normal time.

Then with 77 seconds of injury time on the clock, Robbie Fowler broke Newcastle's hearts with a close-range header to give Liverpool their astonishing win. Last year, 80 seconds of injury time had been played when Stan Collymore scored Liverpool's winner.
The outcome not only put fans of both teams through the emotional wringer, but it also kept alive Liverpool's hopes of winning the title and at the same time just about killed off Newcastle's.

The victory moved Liverpool on to 56 points, a point behind leaders Manchester United with both teams having played 29 matches, and if Liverpool win all their remaining games -- including their home clash with Manchester United on April 19 -- they will win the title.
Liverpool dominated virtually all of Monday's match and appeared to have all three points in the bag when leading 3-0.
They broke Newcstle's stubborn early resistance with goals after 29 and 30 minutes from Steve McManaman and Patrik Berger, and went 3-0 up when Fowler scored two minutes before halftime.
By that stage Newcastle had not had one serious goal attempt, and as late as the 71st minute, Liverpool seemed in no danger whatsoever of losing the points.

Even a mistake by goalkeeper David James when he allowed a shot from Keith Gillespie to squirm through his hands with 19 minutes to go appeared to have handed Newcastle nothing more than a consolation -- until the last frantic minutes.

A raking pass from substitute David Ginola allowed Colombian Faustino Asprilla to score with a volleyed lob over James with three minutes to play and with only 90 seconds left Warren Barton stabbed home a loose ball to somwhow put Newcastle level at 3-3.
But then, with the referee looking at his watch, Liverpool raced upfield, Stig Inge Bjornebye crossed and Fowler leapt to head the winning goal. Fifteen seconds later it was all over.
"I'm delighted to have won it," said a relieved Liverpool manager Roy Evans afterwards.
"I couldn't beleieve it when it went to 3-3. It would have been ridiculous from the way we played and dominated the game if we had gone home tonight without winning it.

"It was a fantastic match, full of emotion and I don't think the final scoreline reflects the game. I must say we didn't defend brilliantly in the second half, but I praised the team for the way they played. The first half hour was some of our best football all season."
Former Liverpool great Kenny Dalglish, back at Anfield for the first time since becoming Newcastle manager in January, admitted his side "shot themselves in the foot".

"You don't come here and give Liverpool a three-goal start," he said, "The first two goals we gave away were very disappointing. You run through the emotions after a game like that, but I don't think the championship is beyond us even though we lost."

Dalglish's cause wasn't helped by his ultra-defensive opening formation when he played 5-4-1 with Asprilla as a lone striker. Newcastle were slightly more adventurous in the second half when Les Ferdinand and Ginola came on as substitutes. But Ferdinand, who has a hamstring injury, only lasted 10 minutes before going off again.
McManaman's opening goal was a classic strike with the ball curled home from the edge of the box with goalkeeper Shaka Hislop grasping at air as the ball nestled in the net. A
minute later Berger scored his first league goal since September when he followed up a Fowler shot that bounced back off a post to ram the loose ball home. Fowler then scored a

superb oportunist goal when he collected a long through ball from Jamie Redknapp, nipping in between Hislop and Belgian defender Philippe Albert, who were left sitting on their backsides and looking at each other in disbelief as Fowler planted the ball in the empty net. Gillespie put Newcastle
back in the match with a shot from the edge of the box that was the first conceded at home by Liverpool in six matches since December 26.
It seemed highly unlikely that the match could ever live up to last season's classic in the corresponding fixture but it did. While the Liverpool fans went home dreaming of their
team's first title since 1990, Newcastle's went home dreaming of what might have been.
Dalglish praised them for their support afterwards, even though one menacingly approached his dugout when they were trailing 3-0 in the first half.

"Even when we were 3-0 down they never stopped backing us. In fact for most of the night, they performed better than the players did. I think the fan who came to see me thought I was registered to play and wanted me to get on," Dalglish even managed to joke. REUTER 102334 GMT mar 97
